name: millbrook
units: metres, Godot axes (x east, y up, z south); yaw = Godot rotation.y in degrees (0 faces +Z); hours are clock hours, t is the day/night cycle position from the layout (lighting.cycle)
tuning_note: Every gameplay number here is a placeholder (sections carry "tuning": true); Scott tunes feel.

unease.gain: act.unease x (0.4 + 0.6 x belief) x (fear_match_mult if the act plays into the fear) x reaction mults

stages.note: The sweet spot: a break scare lands now.

overflow.note: Pushed past their nerve without a break scare: they run for a weak payout.

payout.note: Fright goes to every path whose ability was used; remembrance x villager on_break.remembrance.

suspicion.note: x villager suspicion_rate; reactions fire at their at_suspicion thresholds.

scare_rules.example: Agnes, design plan: overhear her about Button; Flicker candle_1 (dolls+dark fear link), creak the door while she rocks with her back to it, then the doll drop (level 3, run 2): primed + fear + alone + back turned + 3 abilities = Legendary.

villagers.name: Widow Agnes
villagers.personality: Gentle, watchful, talks to the things she loves. Keeps the mill as her late husband Josiah did and sits up late in his rocking chair because the bed feels too big.
villagers.backstory: Her daughter Elsie died young. Elsie's rag doll, Button, still sits on the shelf by the chair.
villagers.fear_story: Button, her late daughter's doll on the mill shelf. She is never quite sure it hasn't moved.

charm.note: garlic and a lavender pouch on her belt; she hangs a sprig

lines: There now, Button. Sit up straight for Mama's mama.
I'd swear I left that doll facing the window.
Don't you look at me like that. Glass eyes, that's all you are.
Elsie never slept without her. I don't sleep much either.
Who moved you? Nobody climbs up to the mill but me.
Funny how a doll can sit so very, very still.
Back on your shelf, and stay there. Please.
mutters.hint: Talks to and about the doll; checks where it is facing.
mutters.note: Overheard when the unmanifested ghost drifts within radius. After 3 lines the journal notes the fear on the villager's card.

suspicious_reactions.line: More light. Elsie always liked the light.
Face the wall, Button. Just for tonight.
Garlic for the doorframe, lavender for the dreams.

on_botch.line: Only the wind in the sails.

villagers.name: Farmer Bram
villagers.personality: Big, warm, proud of never being scared, and therefore jumpy. Laughs off a fright loudly and is a little braver for it next time (the scare_reactions sheet).
villagers.backstory: Works the wheat and pumpkin fields his mother worked. Likes things quiet: pumpkins never bang.
villagers.fear_story: Slammed doors, the square bell, anything that bangs. He jumps, then pretends he did not.

charm.note: horseshoe and pouch on his belt; nails the horseshoe over a door

lines: Quiet night. Good. I like 'em quiet.
That gate bangs one more time, I'm oiling it at midnight.
Thunder or no thunder, I'm not jumping. Not again.
Ma always said a slammed door lets the cold in.
Who's that clattering about? Just the wind. Just the wind.
Pumpkins don't make a sound. That's why I like 'em.
Ring that blasted bell at night and I'll have words.
mutters.hint: Talks about noises, wants things quiet.
mutters.note: Overheard when the unmanifested ghost drifts within radius. After 3 lines the journal notes the fear on the villager's card.

suspicious_reactions.line: Salt. Just in case. Not 'cause I'm scared.

on_botch.line: Ha! Ha. Hah. Nearly had me, that.

schedule.note: Dusk chores at the edge of the wheat, alone, his back to the tall stalks.

villagers.name: Wren
villagers.personality: Quick, kind, nervous; counts steps between lamps and keeps the wick high. Closes the tavern last and looks in on Pip on the way home.
villagers.backstory: The tavern maid. Pip's big cousin: she keeps an eye on Pip while Pip's parents are away at the market town for the season.
villagers.fear_story: The dark. Her lantern going out on the walk home is the worst thing she can imagine.

charm.note: salt pouch on a strap and an herb sprig

lines: Keep the wick high, keep the wick high...
Twelve steps from that lamp to the next. I counted.
Who blew out the lantern by the bridge? Again?
It's only dark. Dark's just the night with its eyes shut.
Should've brought the spare candle. Always bring the spare.
Don't you go out on me now. Don't you dare.
Moon's behind the clouds. Of course it is.
mutters.hint: Talks to her lantern and about light and dark.
mutters.note: Overheard when the unmanifested ghost drifts within radius. After 3 lines the journal notes the fear on the villager's card.

suspicious_reactions.line: Spare candle. In the apron. There.
A line of salt and nothing comes over it.

on_botch.line: Just a draught. Just a draught. Relight it, Wren.

villagers.name: Schoolteacher Marlow
villagers.personality: A skeptic. Sharp, dry, secretly lonely: lives alone, reads late, takes an evening walk to the bridge to prove there is nothing out there. Shrugs off small scares.
villagers.backstory: Came to Millbrook to teach and stayed. Thinks the charm board is bad arithmetic.
villagers.fear_story: Being alone: footsteps in an empty house, a door drifting open, a chair rocking with nobody in it.

charm.note: horseshoe and a salt vial she insists are "decorative"

lines: Superstition is just bad arithmetic.
Charms, salt, garlic... honestly. It's a draught.
Quiet house. Perfectly quiet. That's... fine.
I'll stop by the tavern. Not for the company. For the tea.
Twenty-one desks, and not one of them full after dark.
Is someone there? No. Of course not. Talking to myself again.
A sensible person enjoys her own company. Mostly.
mutters.hint: Insists she likes her own company, then asks the empty room if someone is there.
mutters.note: Overheard when the unmanifested ghost drifts within radius. After 3 lines the journal notes the fear on the villager's card.

suspicious_reactions.line: Loose board. Warped hinge. There's always a reason.
More light to read by. That is all.
Not because I believe it. Because it's tidy.

new_mutters: I saw it. I know what I saw.
Salt on the sill. Don't tell anyone.

on_break.line: That is not... that is NOT a draught!

schedule.note: Reads the charm board at dusk and tuts at it.

villagers.name: Pip
villagers.personality: Curious, brave, delighted by anything strange. Cannot be scared: sees scares and tells everyone, so the legend spreads fastest through Pip. Cute, not cruel.
villagers.backstory: Lives in the family cottage while their parents are away at the market town; cousin Wren looks in every night. Hugs a rag doll and says hello to the ghost.

charm.note: a garlic bulb on a string, mostly for show

lines: Grandma Agnes says a doll's just a doll. I say hello anyway.
I saw the bell wiggle! Nobody believes me.
If you're a ghost, blink twice. ...Was that a blink?
Wren lets me hold the lantern if I'm good.
I'm not scared. I'm keeping watch.
When I see you I'm telling EVERYONE.
mutters.hint: Pip's lines invite the ghost; they hint that Pip will tell everyone.
mutters.note: Overheard when the unmanifested ghost drifts within radius. After 3 lines the journal notes the fear on the villager's card.

rules.when: next dusk, or at once if suspicion >= 1
lines: That's twice now. Garlic it is.
Something likes this one. Not any more.
A charm on it, and that's the end of that.

rules.where: the doorway nearest the botch, else the villager's front door
lines: A line of salt. Let it try now.
Ma swore by salt.
Across the step, nice and thick.

legend.signature: the hauntable kind (or action) used most in Terrified and Legendary scares

templates: {victim} swears the {object} in {place} {trick_past} all by itself. Swears it.
Heard about {victim}? Ran out of {place} like the floor was on fire.
They say {legend} likes {place} best. Don't go there after dark.
{victim} came in white as flour. Wouldn't say what {they} saw. Just kept saying '{object}'.
My nan used to say a {object} that moves on its own is someone remembering you.
The candles in {place} won't stay lit past {hour}. Ask {victim}.
Don't laugh. {legend} got {victim}, and {victim} doesn't believe in anything.
Pip says it's a friendly one. Pip says it waves.
Salt on every step and still the {object} {trick_past}. What's the world coming to.
If you're out late, keep your lantern high and your back to a wall.
